receipts.first_text_witness: 13,000 people are about to wake up rich. Not lottery rich, generational rich, the kind of rich where your grandkids are still living off a decision you made years ago by taking a job at a rocket company and getting paid partly in something most people would have thrown in a drawer and forgotten about. In a few days, that drawer turns into a Nasdaq ticker and the single biggest IPO in the history of the planet goes live. 13,000 people inside that building are set for life. The only question left is whether anybody outside the building gets a seat, too. Whether someone like you with a normal income and a normal brokerage app can grab a piece of this or whether you just watch it happen on the news like every single time before. Because this time something is genuinely structurally different and that difference is the entire reason you're here.
receipts.last_text_witness: curious. Drop a comment and tell me which of the four routes you'd actually take. Are you requesting shares at the IPO price, waiting for the dust to settle and the lockup to hit, going the boring Alphabet route, or just watching the whole circus from the couch with a bowl of cereal? No wrong answers. I read these. Thanks for watching and I'll see you in the next one.
